methodological_questions: How to define and align opponent next-possession after a specific play type?
How to handle end-of-period possessions when next opponent possession may not exist?
What is the sample size and exposure sparsity for individual play types?
What threshold effect size is 'large enough' to assign an AVOID label?
How to incorporate own-sequence lags (prior/subsequent own possessions) in labeling?
What confounding factors (score, time, opponent strength) affect opponent next-possession PPP?
Risk of lookahead bias when using outcome data to label past plays?
Reliability and precision of points-per-possession metrics per play type?
Statistical power to detect meaningful differences in opponent PPP across play types?

failed_approaches.why: Flat lifts collapsed under within-team baseline; team-quality confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type labeling audit: foul leakage and initiation_type mapping
failed_approaches.why: OTHER inflated by 36% foul endings; DRIVE 12pp below foul benchmark; only 0.7% map via initiation_type.
SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP because assisted flag only on makes; leak poisoned simulation.

evidence_establishes: Opponent next-possession PPP after a play type shows very small effects (~0.01-0.02 PPP) for some play types (SF-APPS-075).
Cross-possession carryover effects of play types are flat and confounded by team quality; no reliable decay pattern (SF-CHT-029).
Current inferred play-type labels have systematic errors: high OTHER%, foul leakage, low confidence, and a documented assisted-flag leak that inflates PPP (SF-APPM-014, SF-CHT-025, SF-PAP-096).
evidence_does_not_establish: Magnitude of opponent T+1 effects after fully corrected play-type labels.
Whether own-sequence lag effects exist after adequate confounding control.
What precise effect-size threshold would be considered 'large enough' for AVOID labels.
The statistical power to detect small effects for rare play types in current data.
own_inferences: Even after label corrections, opponent next-possession PPP differences are likely too small (<0.03 PPP) to drive an actionable AVOID label system, unless a very sensitive threshold is adopted.
Confounding by team quality and game context is likely to persist even with within-team adjustments, making causal attribution difficult.
The AVOID label derivation itself risks circularity (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL) and lookahead bias if not carefully split temporally.
A minimal viable test would require redesigned play-type inference, explicit temporal holdout, and a pre-registered effect-size threshold.
uncertainties: Size of opponent T+1 effects after fully corrected labels (post-rewrite, post-fix) is unknown but likely still small.
Stakeholder-defined threshold for 'large enough' is unspecified; without it, the decision rule is arbitrary.
Sample size per play type for reliable PPP estimation may still be insufficient for the rarest play types.
Interaction between opponent next-PPP and own-sequence lags not explored in prior work; could introduce additional complexity.

historical_effect.explanation: Without historical evidence, one might assume that opponent next-possession PPP after a play type can be cleanly measured and that effects might be of practical size. The evidence shows that prior work found small, confounded effects and that the underlying play-type labels are unreliable, making a successful test unlikely without substantial methodological fixes.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels have documented systematic errors (high OTHER%, foul leakage, assisted-flag leak) that bias PPP estimates.
Opponent next-possession PPP is confounded by team quality, score, game context; within-team adjustments may not fully remove.
Prior effect estimates ~0.01-0.02 PPP; detecting such small effects requires tens of thousands of possessions per play type. Rare play types likely underpowered.
If AVOID labels are derived from the same data without temporal separation, future information can leak into the labeling.
AVOID labels are defined by the outcome itself, creating circularity if not validated on independent data.

prior_work.summary: Prior work partially addresses the question: SF-APPS-075 measured opponent next-PPP suppression and found small effects; SF-CHT-029 tested cross-possession memory and found flat, confounded lifts. However, the specific decision rule for AVOID labels and the combined consideration of own-sequence lags have not been directly tested. Multiple artifacts in play-type labeling complicate any direct follow-up.

risks.text: Play-type labels contain systematic errors (OTHER%, foul leakage, assisted-flag leak) that bias per-PT PPP metrics.
Differences in opponent next-PPP across play types may reflect team quality, game situation, and lineup strength rather than a causal effect of the play type.
Effect sizes (~0.01-0.02 PPP) require very large n per play type; the rarest play types (e.g., lob, off-screen) may have insufficient possessions.
If AVOID labels are determined using outcomes from the same season without proper temporal holdout, future information can contaminate the labeling.
The AVOID label is constructed from opponent next-PPP, which is the same outcome used to validate the label, creating circularity unless an independent sample is used.
Testing many play types and two outcome directions inflates false positive risk.
End-of-quarter/game possessions lack a subsequent opponent possession, introducing selection if not handled.
Selecting play types with extreme opponent next-PPP values may lead to regression toward the mean on reassessment.

design.estimand: The causal effect of running play type X on (a) points per possession in the immediately following opponent possession, and (b) points per possession in the immediately following own-team possession, relative to the average after all other play types, adjusted for confounders.
design.unit: Offensive possession that ends and is followed by at least one opponent possession within the same game period.
design.sample: All NBA possessions from 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, excluding end-of-period/game possessions without a subsequent opponent possession. Use only possessions labeled with high-confidence play types after all documented label fixes (post-rewrite, post-fix).
design.power: Assuming true effect sizes of ~0.01-0.02 PPP, detecting a difference of 0.015 PPP at 80% power requires ~50,000 possessions per play type. Common play types (PNR, spot-up, drive) exceed this; rare types (lob, off-screen) likely fall short. Power analysis must be updated after label quality assessment.
design.controls: Score differential, time remaining in quarter, opponent season defensive rating, home/away, rest days, possession start type (made/miss/FT/turnover), team fixed effects (for opponent outcome) and team+opponent fixed effects (for own outcome). Own-sequence lags additionally control for own offensive rating.
design.falsification: Placebo tests: opponent PPP on the second following possession (T+2) where no direct effect is plausible; own PPP on the possession two steps ahead. Sanity checks for label artifacts: verify PPP distributions do not exceed feasible ranges and that assisted-flag leak is absent.
design.multiplicity: Bonferroni correction across all tested play types (8-12) and two outcomes. Complement with Bayesian hierarchical model reporting posterior probabilities with skeptical priors.
design.decision_rule: A play type X receives an AVOID label if: (a) the adjusted posterior probability that its opponent next-PPP effect exceeds +0.03 PPP is >0.95 in a training sample (e.g., 2022-23 through 2024-25), and (b) the effect replicates in the holdout season(s) (2025-26) with directionally consistent point estimate and p<0.05 after correction. Analogous rule for own-sequence lag effects.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26, using corrected play-type labels from the graph database built from play-by-play, with all patches to play_type_inferrer.py applied as of 2026-06-19.

What confounding factors (score, time, opponent strength) affect opponent next-possession PPP?
Risk of lookahead bias when using outcome data to label past plays?
Reliability and precision of points-per-possession metrics per play type?
Statistical power to detect meaningful differences in opponent PPP across play types?

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

reasoning_details.text:
We are in Stage 1: retrieval. The task is to read the research objective and data description, identify research concepts and methodological questions, and retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.

The research question: "Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter." This is about labeling plays as AVOID based on the opponent's points per possession (PPP) on the next possession after running play X. Also, own-sequence lags (i.e., the team's own possession outcomes before or after the play) similarly matter.

We need to identify research concepts and methodological questions. The research concepts likely involve: play-type labeling, opponent next-possession PPP, own-sequence lags, AVOID labels, play-type data quality, and possibly the relationship between play type and subsequent opponent offense. Methodological questions: how to define and measure opponent next-possession PPP after a given play type; how to handle end-of-quarter possessions or transition; sample size and sparsity concerns for specific play types; potential confounding by game situation (score, time, opponent strength); how to determine "large enough" (threshold for AVOID label); how to incorporate own-sequence lags; risk of lookahead bias (deriving labels from future outcomes); data quality issues in play-type labeling itself; reliability of PPP measure; multiple testing if many play types.

We'll craft a query that captures these aspects.

Now, call retrieve_history with appropriate arguments. The function takes research_concepts (list of strings), methodological_questions (list of strings), and query (string). We'll list relevant concepts and questions, and a free-text query.
